texts: mixed: the walk, the station on the Cliff Path, sundown, Year 1 and the one-day gap to the autumn equinox all land, but "the late summer of Year 1" has no licensed form for a season of a stated year, so it becomes a bare late_summer symbol beside Year 1 that nothing can order or relate. Since "one day before the autumn equinox" already fixes the point in the year, dropping the season loses nothing: "In Year 1, one day before the autumn equinox, Meren Tallowhand walked to a station on the Cliff Path at sundown."
good. the lighting carries Meren as the agent, the lantern as what is lit and the station as the place, and "the station" links back to the one introduced in sentence 1.
good. the burning, the lantern as the burner and mire-essence as what is consumed all land, with mire-essence also recorded as a kind of essence.
good. the producing, the lantern and mist-light are all covered.
good. the showing, the mist-light and the night-time are all covered.

mixed: the attracting, the light and the nightmoth group are all there, but "the mist-light" is minted here as a fresh individual with no tie to the mist-light the lantern produced two sentences earlier - a bare substance word cannot be pointed back at by a later "the" - so nothing connects the moths to the lantern. Naming the source in the same clause restores the chain: "The mist-light that the lantern produced attracted nightmoths."
good. the tending, Meren, the lantern and "that night" all land, and the night correctly picks up Year 1 from the opening sentence.
good. the count of seventeen, the lantern as the place and the third watch as the time all sit on one counting event.

mixed: the handful, the gathering and the place all land, but "the Middle Row" gets only its name atom and no kind atom, so nothing records that it is a row - unlike "the Cliff Path" in sentence 1, which this same parse types as a path. Stating the kind beside the name forces it: "A handful of nightmoths gathered at the row called the Middle Row that night."

mixed: the distribution is right - each sky-cat gets its own staying on the cliff-spires that night - but "stayed" has no carrier in that shape, so the parse says no more than "all the sky-cats were on the cliff-spires that night" and the sense of remaining there is lost. An explicit continuation word gives it one: "All the sky-cats were still on the cliff-spires that night."
